ours.name: Southwest Couloir
ours.approach: From the Lupine Meadows trailhead, on the road just south of Jenny Lake, the Garnet Canyon trail climbs into the canyon and breaks down across boulder fields, so pick it up again on the far side and stay on the north side of the creek. At the Meadows camping zone the trail divides: the south fork heads for the saddle between Middle and South Teton, and the way to the Lower Saddle stays on the creek's north side. Climb the south fork all the way to the saddle between Middle and South Teton; do not branch off to the right early. From there the couloir is plainly visible to the west of the summit ridge. ours.descent: This couloir is the usual way down for the whole peak, so a party simply retraces the ascent to the saddle between Middle and South Teton. Go all the way past the saddle before turning east, because the snowfield northeast of it is steep early in the season. fktText: Description This route begins and ends at the Lupine Meadows Trailhead in Grand Teton National Park. Following the Garnet Canyon Trail, it shares the first 4.5 miles of the approach with the route up the Grand Teton. Once it reaches The Meadows, the route takes a left onto the "trail" through the South Fork of Garnet Canyon. Some loose talus and strenuous boulder hopping leads runners up to the saddle between the Middle Teton and the South Teton, at 11,600ft. At the saddle, runners turn right, then follow the classic Southwest Couloir ascent route up to the Middle Teton summit at 12,804ft. After following the same route back down to the saddle, the route continues up the northwestern-most ridge to the summit of the South Teton at 12,514ft. After topping out at the second summit, the route returns down the same way to the saddle between the Middle and the South Tetons. And finally, runners retrace their steps down to the Meadows, rejoin the Garnet Canyon Trail, and then descend the 4.5 miles to Lupine Meadows trailhead in order to finish the route exactly where it started. Overall, the route is about 15.5 miles and 7000 feet of elevation gain trailhead-to-trailhead. Some photos of what to expect along the way can be found here: https://www.stavislost.com/hikes/trail/middle-teton-and-south-teton.
